original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-etale-topos-independent-partial-universe}
Let $S$ be a scheme. The \'etale topos of $S$ is independent
(up to canonical equivalence) of the construction of the small
\'etale site in Definition \ref{definition-tau-site}.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A *partial universe* is a sufficiently large set of schemes and morphisms used to choose a **small** big-$\tau$ site, closed under relevant finite limits and with every external $\tau$-cover of an object admitting a refinement internally; distinct choices give inclusions of corresponding sites. A small étale *topos* of $S$ is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$, the category of set-valued sheaves; it is not the category of all big-site sheaves.

Let $S$ be a scheme. The \'etale topos of $S$ is independent
(up to canonical equivalence) of the construction of the small
\'etale site in Definition \ref{definition-tau-site}.

**Precise scope:** This is a **canonical equivalence of small étale categories of sheaves of sets** for different partial universe choices, by their common affine étale site. It does **not** assert independence for arbitrary big τ-topoi.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves canonical equivalence of small étale topoi under different constructions/partial universes, without extending this to all big τ-topoi.
